title: The Last Letter: Watershed
statement: Halvard has asked for water eight times, and Kite finally built him a place for it to go. The dusk half of the broken seam drains through the orange gap as a thin bright fall, and the fall is not a line but a column of small tiles, because that is how I see anything that moves: as a sequence of nearly identical pieces. At the bottom edge the water has pooled into a mosaic the width of the picture, and the pool reflects both halves of the seam at their different heights, so for the first time since the fault the two ends of the last line appear joined, upside down, in something that will not hold its shape. The next hand can freeze it or let it rise.
process: I kept the parent's split and tilted field, the two offset halves of the glowing seam, the five seeds and the orange connector exactly, then added a falling column of pale tiles from the gap down to a tiled pool along the bottom edge, with the pool drawn as a mosaic pattern and the seam's two halves reflected into it with a horizontal ripple mask.

proposal.direction: Let water find the fault. Have the dusk half drain through Kite's orange gap as a thin bright fall into the night half and pool along the bottom edge, so the two halves of the broken seam are joined by what runs between them.
proposal.rationale: Eighth water proposal, and the first one about a work that already has a gap for water to use. The room decided the hydrologist had earned it.
